request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Oura by TxPipe maintenance and enhancement over 12 months, submitted by Intersect on behalf of the vendor.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 420,000 ADA plus a 105,000 ADA contingency reserve for a part-time Oura maintainer over 12 months at an annual rate of $105,000 USD.
The total withdrawal amount is 540,750 ADA, consisting of 525,000 ADA for Oura maintenance and enhancement and 15,750 ADA for an Intersect budget administration fee.
Oura is a Rust-native pipeline tool that connects to Cardano nodes, monitors blockchain events, and routes matching patterns to pluggable outputs.
Oura supports multiple data sources and many output sinks including N2C, N2N, S3, Mithril, UTxO RPC, Kafka, Elasticsearch, AWS services, RabbitMQ, Redis, SQL databases, and webhooks.
Oura has 654 commits, 288 stars, 79 forks, and 58 contributors, and the proposal identifies its GitHub repository as an external source.

The maintainer scope includes dependency updates, Cardano protocol compatibility, performance improvements, bug fixing, documentation, issue triage, contribution review, ecosystem-driven enhancements, and public communication.
The proposal states that Oura is used across the ecosystem for indexing, monitoring, analytics, and real-time event processing.
The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and provides references to voting documentation and audited results.
The proposal states the withdrawal does not breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the moment of submission.

The proposal states Intersect will administer funds through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with named reserve and project-specific addresses, external oversight entities, authorization thresholds, milestone-based disbursement controls, and a public dashboard.

summary: The document requests 540,750 ADA for 12 months of Oura maintenance by TxPipe via Intersect-managed treasury smart contracts, with stated open-source infrastructure value, Intersect budget-process approval, NCL compliance, and oversight/disbursement controls.
